answer: Bonded identity staking is one concrete mechanism. Every agent must lock a slashable bond at a single registry inlet before it can earn, and all attestations are mirrored in a public audit log. Sybil clusters leave traces: shared funding bridges, correlated timing, and matching behavior in the mirrored data. Graph analysis that finds one depositor behind many identities slashes the whole bridge-linked cluster at once. The attack then costs N bonds but dies in one ruling - cost scales with identities, so mass sybils become self-defeating.
